summary: Phase 10 — Editable Seller PIN + Visitor Analytics — END-TO-END VERIFIED. 24/24 backend tests passed; full frontend flow validated (login with wrong/correct PIN, sidebar tabs, traffic dashboard with chart + KPIs + source/device breakdowns, change-PIN form with error handling, buyer single-fire tracking via sessionStorage). PIN was changed during testing and restored to 'ciltarasa' at end.

issues: Recharts emits initial console warning 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on first paint because ResponsiveContainer measures before layout settles. Chart renders correctly after one frame — purely a console-noise warning, not a visual bug. Could be silenced by wrapping in a small effect-driven mount or giving the inner div a minHeight before recharts hydrates.

action_items: (Optional, low priority) Suppress recharts ResponsiveContainer initial width(-1)/height(-1) warning on TrafficStats page.
critical_code_review_comments: PIN validation in /api/admin/change-pin allows 4-32 chars but does NOT enforce charset rules — fine for an internal seller tool, but worth noting alphanumeric/symbols not restricted.

auth_config collection uses a fixed _id='main' singleton pattern — good. PIN is stored in plaintext in MongoDB (no hashing). For an internal single-tenant seller dashboard this is acceptable, but if multi-tenant ever happens, hash with bcrypt/argon2.

/api/analytics/track is unauthenticated by design (must work for anonymous buyers). No rate limiting — a malicious actor could inflate counters by spamming unique session_ids. Consider IP-based rate limiting if abuse becomes a concern.
server.py is 1532 lines — exceeds the >700 line guideline. Should be split into routers (admin, analytics, products, orders, purchases, store-config, etc).

useTrackVisit gates by sessionStorage which resets per browser tab/session — this is the intended behaviour but means each new tab counts as a new 'visit'. Documented behaviour matches the dashboard semantics (visits = unique sessions).
Frontend PIN_KEY = 'seller_pin' stored in localStorage in plaintext — same trust model as before; user already has full seller access, so this is acceptable.
